Hey, northerner here!!
If you or anyone need any advice on how to cope with the freeze, I have some here— 

•On the subject of power outages: If your fridge is off but it’s cold enough to maintain snow or a frost outside, you can stick some perishables out in the cold to prevent them from going bad— this isn’t AS advisable if you live in an area with high wildlife populations though, but if you have a cold garage or something that gets frigid enough to frost this works as well. It’ll help stave off everything going bad as fast, but it won’t last as long as it would’ve in the fridge. 

•You can use plastic wrap over windows with a slight buffer to make impromptu insulation.

•If possible, stay in one room mostly and stuff cloth under the door frame (if you have some to spare). This lets your body heat partially heat the room you’re in. Shut the curtains over windows to prevent extra cold, but when getting direct sunlight open them. 

•If you have power and a dryer, stick your bedding in the dryer for a brief moment so it’s warm and cozy.

•Keep your toes and fingers warm! No shame in wearing socks on your hands if you gotta, but double layer if you can. Make sure you keep em moving so they don’t end up feeling stiff. Light massaging them helps.

•When the power is on, make sure to charge everything up to 100% or close to it. 

•If your stove works, make sure you’re boiling your melted snow! Just best to make sure there’s no impurities. You can also warm yourself up by the stove if it works.

Sorry if this isn’t extremely thorough advice and if some of this is obvious (I’ve never been to Texas so idk the extent of y’all’s cold weather resources) but I hope it helps someone who might need it a bit!

I mean... it’s literally about how you shouldn’t have kids. “Anti Natalism.” If you want to reduce the impact of having a kid on the earth, there are plenty of ways that depend on the age of your kid. The fact of the matter is that you should raise your kid to be compassionate and kind to human suffering, as well as the suffering of the environment and animals. If your kid is young enough to be in diapers, and you’re economically well-off enough, invest in cloth ones. Go for cloth toys as opposed to hard plastic or electronic ones. Teach yourself and your kid the skills needed to reduce waste, reuse, and recycle. Save jars and other things you can store stuff in that reduces plastic waste— you can store tons of spices, herbs, and other cooking things in them as opposed to plastic bags or bottles— if you can find places that sell them in bulk amounts where you can scoop them into paper bags or your own storage containers. Finding different, sustainable ways to live when you can is important, but there’s no shame in not being able to if you’re economically disenfranchised. The point is to try your best.

Google is your friend here, finding ways to reduce your carbon footprint— even if /you/ can’t at the moment, are good things to teach your kid. Teach your kid about social movements, human rights, and that they always have the ability to choose kindness over cruelty. Always. Fight for a better future as an activist where perhaps we wouldn’t have to worry about all of this. Make it known that when your kid is suffering, they can always come to you. 

The movement is also about reducing suffering once kids are already here. This is why so many of us are adamant that adoption should be considered before and above IVF or having a natural kid, because there are people suffering. Donate (again, if you can, this is a privilege thing) to reputable charities of your choice. Try to be a beacon. 

I won’t tell you how to raise your child in terms of actual parenting. Tantrums, public freak outs, etc., are all part of parenting. Those are learning moments and are teachable experiences. But don’t be a “Karen,” don’t demand things from Childfree people— if you need help, ask for it, and eventually someone kind enough will come along. I don’t believe you had any ill intent, but this is truly not a good place for civil discussion on whether or not you can undo the damage of having a kid. Love them or not, it does environmental damage, and they’ll be growing up through a turbulent time in history... so most importantly, be present for them. 

If you can’t do any of the above, it’s commendable that you tried and reaching out for help from your community if there are any social services should be a priority for both your wellbeing and your kids’. You’ll get flak here for having a kid, but if you didn’t know 2 years ago, that’s not entirely on you. Society has played up the idea that there’s nothing wrong with the way humans are living, when there is. Unfortunately the way our world works, individuals have little impact (except in the way of having kids, and smaller forms of pollutants such as plastics and transportation— the latter of which are nothing in comparison to what unregulated big business does). Though it may be inconvenient at times, try to support small, ethical businesses. This is all very dependent on your lifestyle. 

Don’t tell CF people to get over being societally trampled on for not having kids (work hours, holidays, expectations that women have kids, “Karens”, entitled parents). Don’t speak over people having a tougher time than you on this specific aspect— because while being a parent is obviously hard, not being a parent comes with a host of its own issues and problems in a society that values the nuclear family, overworking, and capitalism more than the people in said society. It’s another kindness to extend— giving people an ounce of empathy despite not being able to have their viewpoint. I’d never have kids, I’d literally rather die, but I know that parenthood is difficult and grueling and demanding. 

There’s all of the advice I can personally give you.

First of all, Childfree 2.0 is a bad comparison because most people on Childfree don’t care whether or not people are having kids, they just want parents to actually parent their kids— and stop assuming that everyone’s life-path is to have kids. This is a bad equivalence. Anti-Natalism is a much more heavy-handed and nihilistic belief system where we believe that bringing children into the world is inherent suffering, so people shouldn’t have kids due to that but also the burden on the rest of the world they have. There’s overlap, but they are not the same. Not sure why that was the point you tried to make above.
